slides.title: Kushmanda, who smiled the universe into being
slides.sub: The fourth form of Durga, worshipped on Chaturthi

slides.title: The first light
slides.body: Her name is traditionally explained as the one who brought the universe, the cosmic egg, into being with a gentle smile when only darkness existed. She is linked to the sun's energy, health and creative power.

slides.title: Eight arms, on a lion
slides.body: She rides a lion and holds a water pot, bow, arrow, lotus, a pot of nectar, discus, mace and rosary. Ash gourd, kushmanda in Sanskrit, is associated with her in some offerings.

slides.text:
सुरासम्पूर्णकलशं रुधिराप्लुतमेव च ।
दधाना हस्तपद्माभ्यां कूष्माण्डा शुभदास्तु मे ॥
slides.translit: Surasampurna kalasham rudhiraplutameva cha, dadhana hastapadmabhyam kushmanda shubhadastu me
slides.meaning: May Kushmanda, who holds in her lotus hands two full vessels, bring me what is good.

slides.title: Durga and Mahishasura: the story on every dais
slides.sub: As the Devi Mahatmya tells it, chapters 2 to 4

slides.title: Heaven is lost
slides.body: Gods and asuras fight for a hundred years. Mahisha, a demon who can take the form of a buffalo, wins, drives the gods out of heaven and makes himself Indra. The gods wander the earth like mortals.

slides.title: A goddess born of light
slides.body: Vishnu and Shiva blaze with anger, and radiance pours out of Brahma, Indra and every god. The light merges and takes the shape of a woman: the combined power of them all, more than any one alone.

slides.title: Each god gives a weapon
items: Indra: a thunderbolt and a bell
Varuna: a conch and a noose
Kala: a sword and a shield

slides.title: The shape-shifter
slides.body: He comes as a buffalo. Caught in her noose, he becomes a lion, then a man with a sword, then an elephant, then a buffalo again. Half out of the buffalo's mouth, he is cut down by her sword.

slides.line: Pala school, 12th century: the same moment, in stone

slides.title: Look closely at the image
slides.body: Durga on her lion, trident in the demon's chest as he climbs out of the buffalo; the lion bites his arm. Bengal adds what the text doesn't: Lakshmi, Saraswati, Ganesha and Kartik beside her.

slides.title: Find this moment at every pandal
slides.ask: Send it to a kid who asks who he is

caption.en:
Durga and Mahishasura: the story behind every Kolkata Durga Puja idol 🦁

It is told in chapters 2 to 4 of the Devi Mahatmya. The buffalo demon takes heaven, and the gods' anger pours out as light that becomes a single goddess. Each god gives her a weapon: Shiva a trident, Vishnu a discus, Himavat a lion to ride.

Mahishasura fights as buffalo, lion, man and elephant. She cuts through every form, and he falls half out of the buffalo's mouth. That is the moment the clay image freezes.

The boon that no man or god could kill him? That comes from later retellings such as the Devi Bhagavata Purana, not from the Devi Mahatmya.

Who did you think the green man at Durga's feet was, as a kid? Tell us in the comments 👇

slides.title: Pandal hopping tips that actually help
slides.sub: Go early or late, go by Metro, one area at a time

slides.title: Pick the right hours
slides.body: Dawn to about 9 am is the calmest. About 6 pm to midnight is peak, longest from Saptami to Navami. After about 1 am the crowds thin out noticeably, though the city stays awake.

slides.title: Go before Shashthi
slides.body: Many big pandals open to visitors from Panchami or even earlier, a good time to see them with fewer people. Opening days vary by committee.

slides.title: Take the Metro, then walk
slides.body: Many lanes near big pandals close to cars in the evening. Sovabazar, Shyambazar, MG Road, Central, Kalighat and Rabindra Sarobar stations are a walk from well-known pujas. Plan one or two areas a night.

slides.title: What to carry
items: Broken-in shoes, for 10 km or more
A water bottle, and refill it
Charged phone and a power bank
Cash in small notes, plus UPI
Light scarf or umbrella, your medicines

slides.title: If someone gets lost
slides.body: Police help desks are usually set up near large pandals and along main roads, and committees run announcement desks. Put a card with your number in each child's pocket and agree a meeting point at every pandal.

slides.title: It's a place of worship
slides.body: Remove shoes where asked and don't touch the protima. Keep flash and selfie sticks away from the altar during puja and aarti, and never stop for photos on stairs or in entry and exit paths.

Go early or go late. That's the big one. Dawn to about 9 am is the calmest, about 6 pm to midnight is peak, and after about 1 am the crowds thin out. Many big pandals open from Panchami or earlier, though opening days vary by committee.

We'd take the Metro and walk, and plan one or two neighbouring areas a night. Carry water, a power bank and both cash and UPI. If anyone gets lost, police help desks are usually set up near large pandals.

slides.title: Narkel naru for Bijoya visits
slides.sub: Fresh coconut, jaggery, cardamom and patience

slides.title: What you need
items: 2½ cups (250 g) fresh coconut, white part only
A tiny pinch of edible camphor (optional)
1 tsp ghee, for greasing your palms

slides.title: Grate only the white
slides.body: Grate only the white flesh; the brown skin makes naru dull. Melt the jaggery, the sugar if using and 2 tbsp water in a heavy, wide pan on low heat for 2 to 3 minutes.

slides.title: Cook till it comes together
slides.body: Add the coconut and salt and cook on low-medium for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring and scraping, until it turns sticky and leaves the sides of the pan as one mass.

slides.title: Do the pinch test
slides.body: Cool a pinch for a few seconds and roll it. If it holds as a ball, it's ready; if wet, cook 2 to 3 minutes more. Stir in cardamom and camphor, then cool 5 minutes on a greased plate.

slides.title: Roll while warm
slides.body: Grease your palms with ghee and roll about 1 tbsp at a time into a smooth ball about 3 cm across. Work fast; it gets hard to shape as it cools. Leave 30 minutes to firm up.

slides.title: Make them ahead
slides.body: In an airtight container they keep 3 to 4 days in a cool room, or up to 10 days in the fridge. Bring them to room temperature before serving.

slides.title: Make a batch before Bijoya
slides.bn: বিজয়ার আগে এক কৌটো বানিয়ে রাখুন

caption.en:
Narkel naru recipe for Bijoya Dashami, the home-made sweet of the Durga Puja visits 🥥

Fresh coconut, jaggery and cardamom, cooked till it holds and rolled by hand. That's it. You'll get about 16, in under an hour.

After Dashami, the plate brought out for Bijoya guests often holds a few of these, and they're back again at Kojagari Lakshmi Puja. Make them ahead: they keep for 3 to 4 days in a cool room, or up to 10 days in the fridge.
